mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment and unemployment improve, it indicates a strong economy, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates may lead to decreased borrowing and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPI indicates inflation, which may lead to monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% in a month
failure_condition: CPI increase but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.
